en: The Philippine Declaration of Independence was signed by exactly 98 Filipinos and one American army officer on June 12, 1898.
The Philippine Senate has exactly 24 elected members, while the House of Representatives can have up to 316 district representatives.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct native languages, but only Filipino and English are designated as the two official languages.
The Banaue Rice Terraces, built by the Ifugao over 2,000 years ago, stretch across 1,036 square kilometers of the Cordillera mountains.
Jose Rizal was only 35 years old when he was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan on December 30, 1896.
Under Philippine law, a citizen must be at least 18 years old to vote, but can run for president at age 40.
The Philippine flag features eight rays on its sun, representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish rule in 1896.
Dr. Fe del Mundo founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines in 1957, providing care to millions of children over 60 years.
The San Agustin Church in Intramuros is the oldest stone church in the Philippines, completed in 1607 after 16 years of construction.
The traditional Filipino barangay, originally a boat called a balangay, typically carried 30 to 100 families before evolving into a village unit.
The 1899 Malolos Constitution, the first republican constitution in Asia, was ratified by delegates and contained exactly 93 articles divided into 13 titles.
The 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution lasted for exactly four days and involved an estimated two million civilians protesting peacefully in Manila.
